summary: Wiki facts rot silently: nobody edited the page, the world just moved. Continuity re-checks each fact against the live web and drafts the fix for a maintainer to approve.

name: Greenlight - Nine-Agent Production Crew
summary: Nine agents turn a screenplay into a film - reading, casting, prompting, shooting, checking their own footage - and quote you the cost and the odds before spending a cent.

page.capture:what_it_does: User drops a screenplay. The system reads it whole, splits it into chapters, breaks chapters into shots, casts characters, writes prompts, generates footage, then inspects what it made: if shot 3 contains a person who should not be there it notices and folds that into the retry instruction. The user presses keep or again. Before any spend it quotes odds: this chapter is 12 shots, ~$4.50, about half will pass first try. Casting is a hard gate; a character reference costs $0.02 while a shot costs $1 and a finished segment ~$20, so every decision is pushed down the cost ladder. Face is an input, look is an output: an uploaded photo is locked as identity while only the style re-renders, and wardrobe is per chapter. Style buttons carry their own success adjustment (photorealistic −10pt vs animation +12/+15pt). Every generation and every keep/again verdict is written to ClickHouse, so once enough similar shots exist the estimate switches from built-in priors to that user's own numbers and says which one you are looking at plus the sample size. After casting, every prompt is exportable.

When a line trips the content filter they generate the shot anyway and move the line into the subtitle layer, so no word of her script changes. Every prompt exports as text, markdown or JSON.
